items.title: Uniform counting of sparse supersets forces symmetry of the statistic
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:sufficent condition symmetry two rows` at source lines 533-537: if a finite set A with a sparse statistic D satisfies |A(D contains J)| = b_{|J|} for every sparse J, then A is symmetric for D. The author's proof (source lines 538-550) converts the hypothesis into symmetry by an indirect route: it first passes to the complementary statistic (line 539), then splits the composition classes into those with a part larger than 2, which are emptied by a two-consecutive-integers argument exploiting both sparsity of D and the definition of respecting a composition (lines 541-543), and those with all parts at most 2, where the complement of the class support is a sparse set with exactly k elements and the hypothesis literally gives the class size b_k (lines 545-547). The final step identifies the sizes as a function of the class alone and invokes the symmetry criterion. The statement mentions only the hypothesis and the conclusion, not the complement or the two-case split.
